lesson_title: The Giant Who Spoils the Average
hook_text: Eight workers earn R6 000. The boss earns R40 000. The company says the average salary is nearly R10 000. True, and a trick.
clip_script: A small firm: eight workers on R6 000 a month and one manager on R40 000. The advert says the average salary is nearly R10 000. Is that a lie? No. Add the nine salaries, 88 000, divide by 9, and you get R9 777. That is the mean, and the mean is true. But line the nine people up by salary and look at the person in the middle: R6 000. That is the median, and it tells you what a worker actually earns. The manager is a giant standing at the end of the line, and a giant pulls the mean towards himself but cannot move the person in the middle. Same with tuck shop spending: eleven learners spent between 5 and 25 rands and one spent 60. Mean 17.25. Median 12. Send the giant away and the mean drops to 13.36 while the median stays at 12. So when someone says average, ask which one. Say it: giants pull the mean, not the median.
visual_style: Nine stick figures in a line on a whiteboard, eight the same height and one towering; the mean slides towards the giant while a marker on the middle figure stays put; the tuck shop numbers repeat the effect with the 60 struck out and the mean falling.
pacing: Advert fast, the arithmetic at speaking pace, the giant image with a beat, the tuck shop repeat fast, the closing question slow.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson for frequency tables, two-way tables, the range and choosing the right measure.
